evidence: Only one top-level module (app.py) contains main application logic with direct imports and function definitions, no clear package structure
Large average fan-out (5.0) indicates functions across modules depend on many external libraries and each other without clear modular boundaries
Highly interconnected procedural functions (e.g., encrypt_aes, encode_uid, create_protobuf) called directly without abstraction layers
Mixing of concerns in single files: web routing, crypto, protobuf, database, async HTTP clients all in app.py
All module contents appear as top-level functions or simple classes (e.g., TokenManager), lacking layering or separation of concerns
absence of explicit ports/adapters or domain boundaries, and no versioning/modularization
risks: Low maintainability due to tight coupling and lack of modularity
Difficulty in testing individual components due to absence of abstractions or dependency injection
Scalability limitations from monolithic procedure calls and shared global state (e.g., tokens)
Security risks from ad-hoc crypto implementations without clear encapsulation
Fragility from shared mutable imports (e.g., protobuf classes used directly across modules)
